extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents); USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive requirements for preparing, submitting, recording, and using assignment and related documents (cover sheets, ownership statements, translations) with the United States Patent and Trademark Office so that assignees may be recorded and may take action in patent applications and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership; assignment must be instrument in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for patent, patents, or any interest therein, shall be assignable in law by an instrument in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 261: assignment must be a written instrument; certificate of acknowledgment (properly executed/apostilled) is prima facie evidence of execution. An assignment is void as against a subsequent purchaser or mortgagee for valuable consideration without notice unless recorded in the PTO within three months from its date or prior to the subsequent purchase or mortgage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment vs license
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between assignment (transfer of entire ownership interest or part thereof) and licensing (transfer of less than entire ownership interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A license is a contract not an assignment even if exclusive. Licenses may be limited by time, geography, or field of use and do not transfer full ownership rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (assignment, application, document, recorded document)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key definitions used for recordation and ownership: Application, Assignment, Document, Office, Recorded document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 37 CFR 3.1 definitions when preparing or interpreting submission and recordation requirements (e.g., 'assignment' = transfer by a party of all or part of its right, title and interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording in assignment records vs recording in application/patent file
rubrics_metrics.description: Two different kinds of recordation: (A) making assignment of record in assignment records (legal notice to public) and (B) making assignment of record in the patent/application file to permit assignee to take action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording in assignment records is ministerial and does not determine validity. To permit an assignee to take action or for a patent to issue to an assignee, the assignment must be recorded or filed for recordation in accordance with 37 CFR 3.11 (see 37 CFR 3.81(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility of assignment records
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment records, digests and indexes are open to public inspection per 37 CFR 1.12, subject to exceptions for confidential records and pre-publication applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies may be obtained for a fee. Assignment records before May 1, 1957 are maintained by NARA. Records related to unpublished/ confidential applications are obtainable only with written authority or petition (and fee). If a document contains both patent and trademark items, the entire document is open if any part is open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents which will be recorded; cover sheet requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments of applications, patents, and registrations, accompanied by completed cover sheets as specified in §§ 3.28 and 3.31, will be recorded. Other documents affecting title will be recorded as provided or at Director's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Order 9424 documents and joint research agreements (or excerpts) will be recorded. Each document submitted for recording must include a single completed cover sheet (Form PTO-1595 may be used). If incomplete, returned per § 3.51.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment document must be a copy (do not submit originals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will accept and record only a copy of an original assignment or other document; originals must not be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copy submitted is illegible, the recorded document will be illegible. The Office will not return recorded documents; ensure legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and legibility requirements for electronic submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submissions must be digitized images in TIFF or another form prescribed by the Director, printable to 8.5x11 or A4 with 1-inch margins and legible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When printed to specified paper sizes, the document must be legible and have 2.5 cm margins on all sides. Follow Director-specified file formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper/facsimile submission formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper/fax submissions must be a copy or extract; only one side of each page may be used; paper size 8.5x11 or A4; 1-inch margins; paper should be flexible, white, non-shiny, durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originals must not be submitted. Facsimile submissions have additional requirements (see fax criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-English assignment documents will not be recorded unless accompanied by an English translation signed by the translator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 3.26: include a signed English translation with the non-English document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of patent or application in assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment must identify the patent by patent number or the patent application by application number; if executed before filing, must identify by inventor names and title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 3.21: International applications must be identified by international application number. If assignment of provisional executed before filing, identify by inventor names and title to avoid mistake. Suggested phrasing to allow insertion of application number when known may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign assignee domestic representative designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee not domiciled in the United States may designate a domestic representative in a written document filed in the USPTO stating a U.S. person's name and address for service of process/notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 3.61: designation should be a separate paper from the assignment and a separate designation should be filed for each patent/application so it can be placed in the appropriate file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee address requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The address of the assignee may be recited in the assignment document and must be given in the required cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assignee address on cover sheet per 37 CFR 3.31.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests to record documents must be accompanied by the appropriate fee; fee charged for each application, patent, and registration identified in the cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 3.41: recording fee set in § 1.21(h) (patents) and § 2.6(b)(6) (trademarks). Exceptions: certain governmental documents meeting criteria in 3.41(b) need not pay the fee if faxed/electronically submitted or mailed per § 3.27 and identified as not affecting title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each cover sheet must contain: (1) name of party conveying interest; (2) name & address of party receiving interest; (3) description of interest conveyed; (4) identification of interests involved (patent/application numbers or indication filed together); (5) correspondence name & address; (6) date executed; (7) signature of party submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic signatures for cover sheets must use specified symbol format (e.g., /Name/) or other Director-specified electronic signature. Patent cover sheets should list number of applications/patents identified and total fee. Cover sheets must not refer to both patents and trademarks on the same sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special cover sheet fields for governmental interests and joint research agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover sheets seeking to record governmental interests must indicate relation to Government and if document does not affect title; joint research agreement cover sheets must identify the document as a 'joint research agreement', the owner, each other party, and execution date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific spaces on PTO form (PTO-1595) when available and include required additional information for trademarks (citizenship, partners) when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing address for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and cover sheets submitted by mail for recordation should be addressed to Mail Stop Assignment Recordation Services, Director of the USPTO, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450, unless filed with new applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests accompanying new applications are addressed to Commissioner for Patents at same P.O. Box; follow § 3.27 to ensure prompt processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile submission allowances and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments and other title documents may be submitted via facsimile and entered into the automated Patent and Trademark Assignment System, provided required items (cover sheet, identified patent/application, and payment) are included; certain documents cannot be faxed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents that cannot be faxed include: assignments filed concurrently with newly filed patent applications; documents with two or more cover sheets; requests for corrections to documents recorded previously; requests for 'at cost' services; resubmission of a non-recorded assignment. The date of receipt for faxed assignments is the date the complete transmission is received. If not recordable, Office will fax back the document with Notice of Non-Recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission requirements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submissions must follow Office-prescribed formats, include necessary cover sheets, and comply with signature and image quality requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 3.24 and Director-prescribed electronic submission specifications; keep credit card info separate per PTO procedures when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of recording (legal notice/protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordation of an assignment provides legal notice to the public; assignments not recorded within statutory time may be void against subsequent purchasers or mortgagees for valuable consideration without notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 261 requires recording within three months from date or prior to subsequent purchase/mortgage to preserve priority. Recordation in assignment records is ministerial and not a determination of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing ownership to take action (37 CFR 3.73(b) statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee must establish ownership by submitting documentary evidence of chain of title and/or specifying reel/frame where recorded, and the submission must be recorded or submitted for recordation for the assignee to take action in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 3.73(b) submission must be submitted prior to or at the same time as the paper requesting action; it may be combined with the action paper. Once complied with, assignee may continue to take action unless ownership changes. Duplicate 3.73(b) statements are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and signing of 37 CFR 3.73(b) statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The 3.73(b) statement must be signed by a person authorized to act on behalf of the assignee; if assignee holds less than entire interest, extent (percentage) must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatures by an officer are presumed to have authority; alternatively the signer may include a statement of authority, or be empowered by organizational resolution; otherwise evidence of authority required. If extent of ownership not set forth for partial assignee, Office may refuse to accept the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may act in patent matters (individual vs partial assignees; composite entity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a single assignee holds entire right, title and interest, that assignee may act alone. If partial assignees/inventors hold interests, all parties holding any portion must act together as a composite entity to conduct prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inventor retains interest, combination of partial assignees and inventor(s) needed to act unless petition under 37 CFR 1.47 granted. Examples in MPEP illustrate changes in who may act as assignments change.

rubrics_metrics.name: When ownership must be established (list of actions requiring 3.73(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership must be established under 37 CFR 3.73(b) prior to or when doing specified actions (e.g., signing a reply to Office action, filing CPA, signing terminal disclaimer, appointing counsel, granting power to inspect, acquiescing to abandonment, consenting to reissue, correction of inventorship, filing certain applications, fee transmittal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP lists many specific instances (see section VII examples). If 3.73(b) submission not present, the action sought will not be given effect; late submission changes the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: When ownership need not be established (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain actions do not require a new 3.73(b) submission when prior ownership statements exist and ownership hasn't changed (e.g., signing CPA when prior statement exists, signing small entity statement, certain affidavits, reexamination requests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP provides examples of actions where 3.73(b) not required; consult specific MPEP sections for each action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple assignees requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where right, title and interest is held by more than one assignee, each partial assignee must provide a 37 CFR 3.73(b) submission, and the extent of each assignee's interest must be set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office uses submitted extents to determine whether action is by entirety of owners. Failure to state extent may result in refusal to accept submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting 37 CFR 3.73(b) statements resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are conflicting 3.73(b) statements, the statement with the latest date normally controls; contested ownership is forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration for resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally the ownership entity that filed the application will be permitted to conduct prosecution; contested parties may consider filing an application under 37 CFR 1.47.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms to be used (PTO-1595, PTO/SB/96)
rubrics_metrics.description: PTO-1595 may be used as the Recordation Form Cover Sheet for patents; Form PTO/SB/96 may be used to establish ownership under 37 CFR 3.73(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the forms' guidelines for completing required fields and include them where appropriate to expedite processing.
